title: 1990 Air Force low-voltage vacuum test of Biefeld-Brown

tellings.quote: For example, in 1990, the Air Force tested a Biefeld-Brown experiment in a vacuum, but they only used 19 kilovolts instead of the megavoltage Brown was using.

plain: In 1990 the US Air Force tested the Biefeld-Brown effect in a vacuum, Michels says. This is the claim, tied to the inventor Townsend Brown, that a high voltage across a device can make it push itself along. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source, and his point is that the test used only 19,000 volts, far below the millions of volts Brown worked with, so it may not have been a fair check.
